subject: Accounting
title: Whistleblowers Who Changed History
description: A 60-second lesson on Whistleblowers Who Changed History.

hook.text: Cynthia Cooper worked nights at WorldCom, digging through records. She found $3.8 billion in fraud.

buildup.text: Whistleblowers—insiders who report wrongdoing—are behind many of the biggest fraud discoveries.

discovery.text: Sherron Watkins warned Enron's CEO. Cooper alerted WorldCom's board. Both were ignored—at first.

twist.text: Before legal protections, whistleblowers were routinely fired, blacklisted, and destroyed.

climax.text: Sarbanes-Oxley and Dodd-Frank now protect and even reward whistleblowers financially.

punchline.text: The bravest accountants don't just count. They speak up.

details.summary: Whistleblowers have been pivotal in exposing the biggest financial frauds—from Enron's Sherron Watkins to WorldCom's Cynthia Cooper. This topic profiles key whistleblowers, the personal risks they took, and how protections have evolved to encourage reporting.
details.whyItMatters: Many of history's biggest frauds were uncovered not by auditors or regulators, but by individuals inside the company who risked their careers and personal safety to speak up.
takeaways: Cynthia Cooper uncovered WorldCom's $11 billion fraud through her own investigation as VP of Internal Audit
Sherron Watkins warned Enron's CEO about accounting irregularities months before the collapse
The Dodd-Frank Act created financial incentives for whistleblowers, with rewards of 10-30% of SEC penalties collected

faq.question: Who are the most famous accounting fraud whistleblowers?
faq.answer: Cynthia Cooper (WorldCom) conducted her own internal investigation to uncover $11 billion in fraud. Sherron Watkins (Enron) wrote a warning memo to CEO Ken Lay. Both were named Time's Persons of the Year in 2002 alongside FBI whistleblower Coleen Rowley.

faq.question: What protections exist for corporate whistleblowers?
faq.answer: Sarbanes-Oxley prohibits retaliation against whistleblowers at public companies. The Dodd-Frank Act created the SEC's whistleblower program with financial rewards of 10-30% of penalties exceeding $1 million. Many states also have their own whistleblower protection laws.
